title: Which numbers leave two over in threes and in fours?
description: A number leaves remainder two on division by three and by four. The video takes the common remainder away, finds the multiples of twelve, and writes one expression for all such numbers.
teaching_notes: One idea: take the common remainder away, and what is left is a multiple of both divisors. Watch for students who find one number and stop.

source: Figure it Out (multiples and remainders, question 4)
video_script.why: The student can find numbers with one remainder on two divisors in the book's example and now does the same for remainder two on three and four.
video_script.substitution: Take the common remainder two away, then use the numbers that both three and four divide.
video_script.anchor: dots grouped in threes and in fours with two dots left over each time, the picture of the What Remains part of the book
video_script.payoff_line: All such numbers are twelve k plus two

final_answer.spoken: two, fourteen, twenty six, thirty eight and so on, all of the form twelve k plus two

maths_rules: n = 3q + 2 and n = 4r + 2, so n - 2 is a multiple of 3 and of 4
numbers in both lists: 12, 24, 36, all multiples of 12
video_script.design: One pile of dots. The two extra dots are set aside, the rest groups exactly in threes and fours, then the two come back as the plus two.

beats.on_screen: small title card From your book; a pile of dots; the words remainder 2 on division by 3 and remainder 2 on division by 4; a blank box for the numbers

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Find a few numbers that leave remainder two on division by three.
<bookmark mark='also'/>They must also leave remainder two on division by four.
<bookmark mark='expr'/>Then write one expression for all such numbers.

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a pile of dots; 2 dots set aside; the rest in full groups of 3 and also in full groups of 4

marks.same: the words the same way as the example in your book appear
marks.aside: two dots slide away from the pile
marks.rest: the rest of the pile forms full groups of three, then full groups of four

narration: <bookmark mark='same'/>We solve this the same way as the example in your book.
Take the common remainder away.
<bookmark mark='aside'/>Here, set the two extra dots aside.
<bookmark mark='rest'/>What is left makes full groups of three, and also full groups of four.

beats.on_screen: Given: remainder 2 on division by 3 and remainder 2 on division by 4
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, a number leaves remainder two on division by three and remainder two on division by four.

beats.on_screen: To find: a few such numbers, and one expression for all of them

marks.find: the two things to find are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find a few such numbers and one expression for all of them.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: take 2 away: n - 2 is a multiple of 3 and of 4

marks.take: n minus two is written under the number n
marks.both: the words multiple of 3 and of 4 appear beside it

narration: <bookmark mark='take'/>Step one, take away the remainder two from the number.
<bookmark mark='both'/>What is left is a multiple of three and also a multiple of four.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: multiples of 3: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18, 21, 24; multiples of 4: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24; in both: 12, 24, 36; all multiples of 12

marks.threes: the multiples of three are listed
marks.fours: the multiples of four are listed
marks.both: twelve, twenty four and thirty six light up in both lists
marks.twelve: the words multiples of twelve appear

narration: <bookmark mark='threes'/>Step two, list the multiples of three. They are three, six, nine, twelve, and so on.
<bookmark mark='fours'/>The multiples of four are four, eight, twelve, sixteen, and so on.
<bookmark mark='both'/>Twelve, twenty four and thirty six are in both lists.
<bookmark mark='twelve'/>These are all multiples of twelve.

marks.back: the two is put back on both sides: n equals twelve k plus two
marks.vals: k equal to zero, one, two and three give two, fourteen, twenty six and thirty eight

narration: <bookmark mark='back'/>Step three, put the two back. The number is twelve k plus two.
<bookmark mark='vals'/>Putting in k as zero, one, two and three gives two, fourteen, twenty six and thirty eight.

marks.fourteen: fourteen is split in threes and in fours, each with two over
marks.twenty: twenty six is split in threes and in fours, each with two over

narration: <bookmark mark='fourteen'/>Step four, put the numbers back in the question. Fourteen is three times four plus two, and four times three plus two.
<bookmark mark='twenty'/>Twenty six is three times eight plus two, and four times six plus two.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 2, 14, 26, 38, and so on: all numbers of the form 12k + 2
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Such numbers are two, fourteen, twenty six, thirty eight and so on.
All such numbers are twelve k plus two.
